column1: # p14 platform_profile {balanced,performance} A/B at fixed DPM high, 2026-08-22.
# HOST IS A REPLACEMENT MAINBOARD -- see dpm-results.tsv for the full provenance note.
# Server: llama-test.service (the p14/disk-prompt-cache fork), same as p16s-bench-results.tsv.
# Harness: bench-prof.sh, 3 interleaved rounds, GPU DPM pinned to high throughout.
# Profile switched with powerprofilesctl, not a raw sysfs write.
# Q: the board makes 375 PP where the P16s made 488 at the same 2900 MHz on the same DIMMs.
#    Is it running a lower cTDP? platform_profile is the knob that would show it.
# A: NO. balanced 375.2 vs performance 373.8 -- -0.4%. README's "Ruled out" verdict on
#    platform_profile survives the board swap.
# The per-round drift under sustained dpm-high (it heats, PP decays ~1.4%):
#     round 1   379.1 PP   45.0 W   80 C
#     round 2   376.6 PP   49.0 W   90 C
#     round 3   373.7 PP   49.1 W   94 C
# NOTE -- an earlier version of this header concluded from the above that the board is
# thermally limited. THAT WAS WRONG and is retracted. The side-by-side against
# p16s-bench-results.tsv at DPM auto settles it: identical 24.0 W, p14 clocks 10% HIGHER
# (2169 vs 1971 MHz), runs 4 C COOLER, and is still 18.5% slower. Throughput-per-clock is
# down 23-26% in BOTH DPM arms -- invariant to power state, which is not how a thermal limit
# behaves. The lower power at dpm-high is a SYMPTOM: a GPU at 100% busy and the same clock
# drawing 15% less power is stalling, not throttling.
# Current reading: the board is MEMORY-STALLED. Suspect the memory path after the DIMM move
# (training, channel interleave, fabric/uclk ratios). Ruled out: platform_profile, thermal,
# power cap, DPM, governor, GPU identity (0x150e rev 0xd1, 32 SIMDs = 16 CU), all GPU clock
# domains (mclk 2800, fclk 1960, socclk 1472 -- all at max), llama.cpp build, Mesa version.
# HARNESS GAP: mclk/fclk/socclk were never sampled on the P16s, so they have nothing to be
# compared against. Sample all four clock domains next time, not just sclk. See TODO item 11.
